serialFormats.description: 10-character Lennox serial (1973 to present): 2-digit plant/factory code, 2-digit year, 1 month letter (A-M skipping I), 5-digit production sequence. Used on residential and commercial equipment alike.
sources: Building Intelligence Center, 'Lennox HVAC age' (building-center.org/lennox-hvac-age/) - style 1 examples 1606B13871 (Feb 2006) and 5899L17212; positions 1-2 plant, 3-4 year, 5 month letter
PickHVAC, 'Lennox HVAC Age: Serial Number Decoding' (pickhvac.com/hvac/age-serial-number/lennox/) - month letters A-M skipping I; 5806E12345 = plant 58, May 2006
Parts Town, 'Lennox Serial Number Lookup' (partstown.com/cm/resource-center/guides/gd2/lennox-serial-number-lookup) - plant code list 51/53/54/55/56/58/63
hvacdecoder.com Lennox serial number decoder - agrees on plant/year/month-letter layout
notes: Year = characters 3-4 (two digits). Pivot 70: 73-99 -> 1973-1999, 00-69 -> 2000s. The format has been in continuous use since 1973 so a two-digit year is unambiguous within the era.
Month letter skips I: A=Jan ... H=Aug, J=Sep, K=Oct, L=Nov, M=Dec. A serial with I or N-Z in position 5 is not this format (re-read the plate).

Plant map covers only the codes documented by the secondary sources; the building-center example 1606B13871 carries plant 16, which is not in that list. Unknown plant codes still decode (year/month) but the plant is reported as the raw code.

Confidence is medium (three independent secondary decoders agree); Lennox's own 'Model and Serial Nomenclature' PDF (lennox.com/lib/legacy-res/pdfs/lennox_model_and_serial_nomenclature.pdf) is the primary source but could not be read in this session - promote to high once a warranty lookup on LennoxPros (Resources > Warranty lookup by serial) confirms three dated examples.
Residential and commercial Lennox units share this serial style; the difference is only the plant code (commercial rooftops are typically 56 Stuttgart AR or 58 Marshalltown IA).
Cross-check: the compressor date code and the refrigerant printed on the nameplate (R-22 before ~2008-2010 on rooftops, R-410A after, R-454B from 2025) should agree with the decoded year.

serialFormats.description: 9-character Lennox serial reported for the late 1970s to early 1990s: a letter, five digits, three letters; characters 2-3 are the year, the second-to-last character is the month letter.
sources: PickHVAC, 'Lennox HVAC Age: Serial Number Decoding' (pickhvac.com/hvac/age-serial-number/lennox/) - 'Style #2': letter + 5 numbers + 3 letters, 2nd/3rd characters = year (86 = 1986), second-to-last letter = month (D = April)
notes: LOW CONFIDENCE: only one secondary source (PickHVAC) describes this style, and Building Intelligence Center states the 10-character plant/year/month style has been used exclusively since 1973 - the two sources disagree on whether this style exists. Treat any decode as a hint and confirm the year from the nameplate style and refrigerant (R-22 era).
The two examples are CONSTRUCTED to exercise the published rule; they are not real nameplates. Replace with dated nameplate photos when available.
The month-letter map (A-M skipping I) is assumed to match the 1973+ style; PickHVAC only confirms D = April.
No collision with the 10-character style: this style starts with a letter and is 9 characters long; the 1973+ style is all digits except position 5.

controls.name: Lennox Prodigy (M2) / Prodigy 2.0 (M3) unit controller
controls.description: Microprocessor unit controller with LCD and push-button menu fitted to Energence (and late Strategos) rooftops: Prodigy M2 (2009-2013, doc 506215-01 / application guide 506457) and Prodigy 2.0 M3 (2013+, setup guide 507241-07, application guide 507242-07). Alarm/event codes are numeric; selected alarms close the service relay contacts (DO1).

faultCodes.meaning: Blower alarm (S52 blower airflow proving) - repeated code 5 alarms result in the 'STRIKE 3 ON BLOWER' lockout.
likelyCauses: Blower not proving airflow (broken/slipping belt, blower motor or VFD fault, S52 airflow switch or its tubing)
Dirty filters / closed dampers starving the blower
checks: Confirm blower rotation and belt condition; check motor amps against nameplate FLA
Verify S52 airflow switch closes on blower start (check tubing and switch setpoint)
Check blower motor overload / VFD status
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 (M3 Unit Controller) Application Guide 507242, Table 65 'Prodigy 2.0 Alarm and Event Codes' (ManualsLib 1251298 p.147-156)
faultCodes.notes: Meaning paraphrased from the guide's 'STRIKE 3 ON BLOWER' entry, which references multiple alarm code 5 events; verify the exact wording in Table 65.

faultCodes.meaning: Lockout is active - multiple alarm code 5 (blower) events detected. Can be manually cleared through the user interface.
checks: Fix the underlying blower/airflow fault, then clear the lockout from the controller UI (Service menu)
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 (M3 Unit Controller) Application Guide 507242, Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298)

diagnosticTips: Alarms and events are listed in the Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65/66 (Alarm and Event Codes); alarms marked with * close the service relay DO1. Prodigy (M2) uses Application Guide 506457.

Lockouts (e.g. STRIKE 3 ON BLOWER, compressor strike-3 lockouts) are cleared manually through the controller's user interface (Service/Settings menu) after the fault is corrected; cycling power also clears most lockouts but not the stored alarm history.
Use the LennoxPros 'Error Code Lookup' tool (Technical Tools on LennoxPros.com or the LennoxPros app) to look up any Prodigy alarm number with troubleshooting steps.
sources: Lennox Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242-07 (ManualsLib 1251298 pages 147-156, Table 65 Alarm and Event Codes)
LennoxPros 'The New Error Code Lookup Tool' (m.lennoxpros.com/news/error-code-lookup-1810)

controls.name: Lennox CORE Control System (M4 unit controller) and CORE Lite
controls.description: Current Lennox unit controller (M4) with a colour touchscreen-style menu on Model L, late Energence and other rooftops; CORE Lite is the reduced version on Xion. Numeric alarm codes with a display message and an event action (cause + solution) are listed in the CORE Application Guide 485115 Table 11 'CORE Control System Alarm and Event Codes'.

faultCodes.meaning: ERRATIC POWER (single phase units) - power loss for two cycles; dirty or low-quality power.
likelyCauses: Loose or corroded line/control power connections
Utility voltage sags, generator or poor power quality
checks: Check and tighten power connections at the disconnect, contactor and controller
Measure supply voltage under load and compare to nameplate range
faultCodes.source: Lennox CORE Control System (Unit Controller) Application Guide 485115, Table 11 Alarm and Event Codes

faultCodes.meaning: Strike3 High Press S4 Open Comp - compressor 1 locked out after three high-pressure switch (S4) trips. Event action: check charge, fans and coil; use the Service menu to clear lockouts.
likelyCauses: Outdoor fan not running (motor, capacitor, contactor, fan relay)
checks: Measure head pressure vs. outdoor ambient (condenser split) and subcooling
Verify outdoor fan operation and amps
Inspect/clean condenser coil
Check S4 continuity and trip point
faultCodes.source: Lennox CORE Control System (Unit Controller) Application Guide 485115, Table 11 (alarm 13*, service relay closes)

diagnosticTips: Alarm codes are shown on the CORE display with a message and an event action; the full list with cause/solution is Table 11 of the CORE Application Guide 485115 (and the CORE Lite guide 508676-01). Model L specifics are in the CORE Information Guide 508111-03.
Compressor lockouts (strike-3 alarms) are cleared from the Service menu after correcting the fault.
Initial configuration, test/service modes and network setup are in the CORE Unit Controller Setup Guide 508111-01.
The LennoxPros Error Code Lookup tool covers CORE alarm numbers.

controls.name: Lennox IMC (Integrated Modular Control) M1-x unit controller
controls.description: Board-mounted microprocessor controller (A55, versions M1-4 through M1-8) on L Series and S-Class (Strategos) gas/electric, electric/electric and heat pump rooftops (c. 1997-2012). Displays and stores 2-digit error codes; configured by DIP switches; optional IMC BACnet module and L Connection network.

faultCodes.meaning: S4 high pressure switch (compressor 1) is open.
likelyCauses: High head pressure: dirty condenser coil, outdoor fan failure, overcharge, non-condensables
checks: Check head pressure vs. ambient, outdoor fan operation, coil cleanliness
Verify S4 continuity when pressure is below the reset point
faultCodes.source: Lennox IMC M1-7 Version 5.02 Integrated Modular Control manual, Table 4 error codes (manualzz mirror)

faultCodes.meaning: First-stage high pressure switch has opened three times (default) and the control has de-energized the compressor (lockout).
likelyCauses: Repeated high-pressure trips on compressor 1 (see code 12)
checks: Correct the high-pressure cause, then reset the IMC (power cycle or reset per the IMC manual) to clear the lockout
faultCodes.source: Lennox IMC M1-7 Version 5.02 Integrated Modular Control manual, Table 4 error codes (manualzz mirror)

diagnosticTips: Error codes are shown on the A55 IMC board's 2-digit display and stored for later recall (IMC manual Table 4 and Figure 16 list every code; M1-7 v5.02 is at webmanuals.lennoxeurope.com / manualzz 'IMC V7').
Codes seen in the field but not transcribed here: 59 (sensor-related), 73/74, 92 (DIP-switch configuration) and 93 - look them up in Table 4 or the LennoxPros Error Code Lookup tool before acting.
The IMC shunts the low-pressure switches (S87/S88) during compressor start until pressure stabilizes, so a low-pressure trip logged after the delay is a real refrigerant/airflow problem.
Lennox Technical Support 800-453-6669 is referenced in the IMC documentation.

components.notes: Lennox convention; verify. Prodigy 2.0 and CORE also perform phase/voltage detection in software (alarm 1 erratic power).

safetyDevices: S4 / S7 high pressure switches (auto-reset; controller counts strikes and locks out after three - alarm 13 on IMC/CORE)
S87 / S88 low pressure switches (shunted by A55 during start-up)
S10 primary limit and rollout switches on gas heat sections
S52 blower airflow proving switch (Prodigy 2.0 alarm 5 / STRIKE 3 ON BLOWER)

terminalLabels.R: 24 VAC hot to thermostat (Lennox convention - verify on unit controller)
terminalLabels.DO1: Service relay output (closes on selected alarms; Prodigy 2.0/CORE)

sequenceOfOperation: Cooling (unit-controller units): on Y1 (or network demand) A55 energizes the blower (B1) and, after proving airflow via S52, energizes compressor contactor K1 (compressor B3) and the outdoor fan (B4); low-pressure switches S87/S88 are shunted during start-up. Y2 brings on the second compressor/stage. High-pressure switch S4/S7 trips de-energize the compressor; three trips = strike-3 lockout (alarm 13).

Heating (gas): on W1 the ignition control A3 checks limits (S10, rollout) and the combustion-air pressure switch, runs the combustion blower prepurge, energizes the spark/igniter and gas valve GV1, and proves flame; the blower starts after the heat-on delay. W2 adds the second heat stage. Repeated ignition failures produce a heat lockout alarm on the unit controller.
Economizer: A2 / unit controller modulates outdoor-air dampers for free cooling when outdoor conditions are suitable; mechanical cooling is staged behind it.
notes: Only A55, K1, S4, S87 and S88 were confirmed against Lennox documents this session (wiring diagram 538043-03 and service literature 100087); the remaining designators follow the Lennox commercial numbering convention (A = controls/boards, B = motors, K = relays/contactors, S = switches, RT = temperature sensors, T = transformers, GV = gas valves) and must be checked against the legend printed on the unit's wiring diagram (inside the control compartment door).
The sequence of operation is generic to Lennox unit-controller rooftops; the model-specific sequence is in the unit's service literature ('Unit Information') and IOM.
Landmark/Raider units without a unit controller use conventional 24 V thermostat wiring through relays and a defrost/ignition board.
sources: Lennox Commercial Wiring Diagram 538043-03 (lennox.com/dA/6a08183ad7/538043-03.pdf) - K1 single pole contactor, S4 high pressure switch
Lennox Unit Information service literature 100087 (lennox.com/dA/c7c4a21f62/100087.pdf) - S87/S88 low pressure switches wired to A55; A55 shunts LP switches during start-up
Lennox Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 (S52 blower alarm reference)

commonIssues.symptom: Compressor keeps running / will not shut off during high outdoor humidity on a Prodigy 2.0 unit
likelyCauses: Dehumidification (Humiditrol / reheat) or humidity-based control parameter keeping mechanical cooling on when the outdoor humidity sensor reads above the setpoint (reported field pattern, forum-level evidence)
Faulty or mis-scaled outdoor/return humidity sensor
checks: Check the humidity sensor readings on the Prodigy display against a calibrated meter
Review dehumidification settings and disable to confirm the behaviour changes
Check Prodigy firmware level and controller parameters against the setup guide
sources: HVAC-Talk thread 'Lennox prodigy 2.0' (hvac-talk.com/threads/lennox-prodigy-2-0.2187821/)

commonIssues.symptom: Loss of communication between the Prodigy/M2 controller and the network or display; controller replaced more than once
checks: Check 24 VAC supply and grounding at A55
Inspect network daisy-chain wiring, polarity and termination
Verify firmware and replace the controller only after wiring and power are proven
sources: HVAC-Talk threads 'Lennox Prodigy 2.0 Issue' and 'Lennox Prodigy Board'

commonIssues.symptom: Compressor locked out on high pressure (IMC code 13 / CORE alarm 13 Strike3 High Press S4)
checks: Compare head pressure to outdoor ambient (condenser split) and subcooling
Confirm outdoor fan runs and draws normal amps
Clean coil; check S4 trip/reset points
Clear the lockout from the Service menu (CORE/Prodigy) or reset the IMC after repair
sources: Lennox CORE Application Guide 485115 Table 11 (alarm 13 event action: check charge, fans and coil)
Lennox IMC M1-7 manual Table 4 (code 13)

commonIssues.symptom: Nuisance low-pressure trips at compressor start in cold weather
likelyCauses: Low refrigerant charge or restricted airflow (dirty filters, iced coil) - the A55 controller shunts S87/S88 only during start-up, so trips after the delay are real
checks: Verify suction pressure after the start-up shunt period
Check filters, blower operation and evaporator coil
Check S87/S88 continuity and setpoint
sources: Lennox Unit Information service literature 100087 (A55 shunts low pressure switches during start-up)

commonIssues.symptom: Blower alarm / STRIKE 3 ON BLOWER lockout (Prodigy 2.0)
likelyCauses: Blower motor overload or VFD fault
S52 airflow switch or tubing fault
checks: Inspect belt tension/condition and sheave alignment
Measure blower motor amps vs. FLA; check VFD fault log
Verify S52 switch operation and tubing
Clear the lockout from the UI after repair
sources: Lennox Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (STRIKE 3 ON BLOWER)

commonIssues.symptom: Economizer not bringing in outdoor air / stuck at minimum or fully open
likelyCauses: Failed or drifted outdoor/return sensors (temperature or enthalpy)
checks: Command the damper through the controller's test mode and watch travel
Check actuator power and feedback
Compare sensor readings to a reference thermometer/psychrometer
Review economizer setpoints in the controller
sources: PNNL 'Best Practices for Air-Side Economizers Operation and Maintenance' (stuck dampers, sensor failures, linkages, actuators, settings)
Lennox Economizer for Energence rooftop units instruction (manuals.plus mirror)

commonIssues.symptom: Unit not cooling - general packaged rooftop failures
checks: Check capacitor uF and contactor contacts
Inspect belts and blower motor amps
Inspect/clean condenser coil
Check superheat/subcooling for charge
Inspect economizer damper position
sources: Alex Air & Heating 'Rooftop HVAC Unit Repair' and Oxmaint 'RTU Not Cooling' - generic rooftop failure patterns (not Lennox-specific)

support.literatureSearchHint: On LennoxPros.com go to Resources > Document Library and search by the full model number (e.g. LGH120H4BH1G) or serial number; filter by 'Installation Instructions' (IOM), 'Service Literature' (Unit Information, includes wiring legend) or 'Wiring Diagram'. PDFs are hosted at tech.lennoxintl.com and lennox.com/dA/. Engineering handbooks with the model number identification page are named ehb_<family>_*.pdf (e.g. ehb_lgh_cbox_2103.pdf).
support.notes: The LennoxPros Error Code Lookup tool (Technical Tools) decodes Prodigy/CORE/IMC alarm numbers with troubleshooting steps.

notes: Nameplate: the factory MODEL NO. and SERIAL NO. are on the unit rating plate on the compressor/control side; the serial is always 10 characters on 1973+ equipment. Catalog numbers such as L1318 or 45W08 are LennoxPros stock numbers, not model numbers.

Lennox rooftop nomenclature (2009+) is positional: brand letter, unit type (G gas/electric, C electric/electric, H heat pump, D dual fuel), generation/family letter, 3-digit nominal cooling MBH, efficiency (S/H/U), refrigerant (4 = R-410A, 5 = R-454B), blower type, heat input (gas S/M/H, N none), minor design digit, voltage (P 208-230/1, Y 208-230/3, G 460/3, J 575/3), then optional factory-installed option codes.

Family names verified this session: L Series LGA/LCA/LHA (and LGC/LCC), Strategos SGA/SCA + SGH/SCH/SCC, Energence LGH/LCH, Model L LGT/LCT/LHT/LDT, Xion LGX/LCX/LHX (not XGA/XCA), Landmark KGA/KCA/KHA + KGB/KCB/KHB/KDB, Raider ZGA/ZCA/ZHA + ZGB/ZCB/ZHB, T-Class TSA/TPA/TAA. CBA/CBH/CBX are residential air handlers; 'Elite' ELS/ELC and 'Enlight' could not be verified.

Web search budget ran out before the Prodigy/CORE/IMC alarm tables and the 38Z29 model number identifier sheet could be transcribed; controls coverage is therefore 'partial' with only source-confirmed codes, and most electrical designators are flagged as convention-based. These are the first items to expand on the next review.
Lennox Commercial Controls System (LCCS) and L Connection Network are BAS/network layers, not unit controllers; alarm codes come from the unit controller (IMC/Prodigy/CORE).
